# SPD-006 — Ledger database spike: what replaces markdown-v0

## Brief
Eric asked for the ledger database spike, the first real ticket after bootstrap. The brief is Appendix A of `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-09-12-spud-design.md`: answer eight questions with evidence (store, topology, schema, concurrency, migration, glue language, enforcement, fleet view and reports) and write `docs/spikes/2026-09-12-ledger-database.md` with the ten sections named there. The spike decides what replaces `markdown-v0`; it does not implement it. No code files; DDL in a code block is spec, not code. Eric's stated need from 2026-09-12 (question 8) is in scope: click a ticket and see the lead, every spudagent under it with persona, model, and status, and a summary of what they worked on and built.

Done when: the spike file exists with all ten sections in order, each of the eight questions has an evidenced answer and one recommendation rather than a menu, measurements come from this machine and say so, sources are cited, the researcher's proposals and open questions for Eric are recorded, the outcome is recorded here, and the work is committed.

## Size, persona and model decision
One researcher, who may build a team of up to two, because the brief says so and the work has separable evidence-gathering parts (prior-art survey, native-facts lookup, machine measurements) around one indivisible synthesis.

- Lead: [[SPUD-006/Vitelotte|Vitelotte]] (01, researcher, **fable**). Default tier for the persona, no override. Eric specified researcher on fable, and the spike is the decision every later ticket builds on: data model, concurrency, and enforcement are the "expensive if wrong" category.
- Optional children, Vitelotte's call: a scout on haiku for the Minilla prior-art survey or the latency and concurrency measurements, and/or a `claude-code-guide` contractor (recorded with `persona: contractor`, `agent_type: claude-code-guide`, explicit model) for native facts about hook payloads and what the Agent tool returns. Depth remaining below Vitelotte is 1, so any child gets "no sub-agents".

Concurrency: at most 1 + 2 = 3 of 9.

## Outcome
Shipped `docs/spikes/2026-09-12-ledger-database.md` (10,893 words): the ten mandated sections in order, one recommendation per Appendix A question, every number measured on this machine on 2026-09-12 with the method stated, every native fact cited to official documentation. Verified by Spud: spike read in full, all three team files consistent (IDs, parents, nesting, Outcomes, real timestamps), `git status` shows only the spike and the SPUD-006 folder, no code files.

The recommendation, in one paragraph: SQLite in WAL mode, one file at `.spud/ledger.db` in Spud's home, gitignored, found through `SPUD_HOME` so worktrees resolve to the one real database; one database for every project with a `projects` table; tables `projects`, `tickets`, `members` (the team tree, lineage as a materialized path, every limit a `count(*)` inside the insert transaction), `spawn_requests`, append-only `events`, `handoffs`, `proposals` and `proposal_decisions`, `name_pool`, `renders`; every process opens the file itself with `busy_timeout = 5000` and `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` (0 lock errors at 9 and 30 concurrent writers; 995 and 1056 errors in the two trap configurations), no daemon and no MCP writer; import the markdown once, render it always, markdown committed and database ignored, `user_version` migrations; Python 3.14 stdlib as `bin/spud` run with `python3.14 -I -S` (hook-shaped cold start 17 to 18 ms against Node 26 ms and Bun 13 ms); Laws 3, 4, 6, 7 plus the path and finishing rules move into hooks and the CLI, with `agent_id` bound to a member through `tool_use_id` from `PreToolUse(Agent)` and `PostToolUse(Agent)`; Eric's per-ticket card is a generated `## Team` table plus `![[Fleet.base#Team]]` filtered `ticket == this`, and reports render from events.

Findings worth Eric's eye beyond the recommendation: the harness gives every hook inside a subagent its `agent_id`, and Spud's own calls carry none, so identity needs no prose; `SubagentStop` can hold a child that returns without a Result; background subagents cannot answer permission prompts, so the CLI needs an allow rule; the Agent tool's telemetry (`totalTokens`, `totalDurationMs`, `totalToolUseCount`) is documented and was captured first-hand (Vitelotte 408,675 tokens over 33.6 minutes, Elba 202,844, Dakota 67,198).

Left: Eric's nine open questions in the spike's last section, each with Vitelotte's recommendation. [[SPD-007]] to [[SPD-014]] are queued and wait on them. Not measured: Obsidian's pickup of files written by another program while the vault is open; the first `spud render` is the check.
